label: GO step, choosing a1 after a rewarded trial
explanation: Fires only at the GO step (D1 and D2 essentially never), when the agent is about to choose a1 (model_act == 1, the agent own policy output, so no future info) and the previous trial was rewarded. It is an a1-choice feature: GO & a1 alone gives F1 0.81 / mass recall 0.97, and adding prev_reward == 1 raises precision to 0.97 (dev F1 0.87, mass recall 0.94). Magnitude increases with a1 policy confidence (choice logit > 8 holds 77% of mass) and with runs of consecutive rewarded a1 trials, largely while S1 is good. The misses are weak activations, about 0.1-0.35 of max, at a1 GO steps after unrewarded trials, plus rare faint firing at a2 GO steps. It does not fire at a2 choices with any real strength (3% of mass), and it does not fire on D1/D2 steps.

issues: The phase claims hold. D1 mass is 0.00003 and D2 has zero activations. GO holds 100% of the mass, spread evenly over rel -3..+1. The original predicate's test scores reproduce exactly (P 0.967, R 0.781, F1 0.864, mass recall 0.934).

The reward framing points at the wrong conditioning variable; what matters is the state the previous trial reached. GO & a1 & prev_reward==1 & prev_state==1 has test precision 1.000. GO & a1 & prev_reward==1 & prev_state==2 (rewarded at S2, then the agent picks a1) has precision only 0.48 and 0.26% of the mass. That is a systematic false-positive class: the false-positive windows in the misses output are dominated by the previous trial being 'S2R rewarded'.

The misses after unrewarded trials are not uniform. GO & a1 & prev_reward==0 & prev_state==1 fires 74% of the time (2.7% of mass). GO & a1 & prev_reward==0 & prev_state==2 fires 4.5% of the time (0.03% of mass). So the feature fires on a1 after the previous trial reached S1 whether or not it paid, with weaker activations when it did not pay.

The 'rare faint firing at a2 GO steps' is not scattered noise. GO & a2 & prev_state==1 & prev_reward==1 is active 89% of the time (weak, 2.9% of mass). So the faint a2 firing also follows a trial that reached S1 and was rewarded.

An observed-only predicate that conditions on the previous reached state does better. GO & a1 & ((prev_reward==1 & prev_state!=2) | (prev_reward==0 & prev_state==1)) scores test F1 0.899 (P 0.963, R 0.842, mass recall 0.959), against 0.864 for the original. prev_state is -1 on each window's first trial (rel -3), which is why the condition is written as != 2.

The label is mostly right (GO, choosing a1, magnitude driven by S1 being rewarded). But 'after a rewarded trial' overclaims reward in general: a1 after reward at S2 does not drive it reliably, while a1 after an unrewarded visit to S1 does, weakly.
